style: Layered cut-paper illustrations with exact paper-color energy diagrams
provider: Built-in image generation and deterministic SVG diagrams
groups: Follow a collision and a circuit
note: Pictures and arrows are models, not measurements. Repeated ball positions are successive observations, not multiple balls. Speed comparisons use the same mass and equal time intervals. Collision panels show an idealized equal-mass, straight-on case; actual results vary. Electric current means flow of charge, not energy itself. Heat flows spontaneously from warmer to cooler overall; powered heat pumps can transfer heat the other way. Energy is conserved while changing form and spreading out. Light cones, sound arcs and warmth wisps are illustrative conventions, not visible solid material. Sorting follows the specific journey named on each card, although devices can transfer energy in several ways. Appliance pictures are observation examples; practical circuit work uses teacher-approved low-voltage batteries. Do not handle hot liquids or household wiring for these activities.
